Which Turkish provinces lead in white marble, travertine and onyx blocks/slabs?

Afyonkarahisar—especially the İscehisar corridor—leads Türkiye in white, grey, and violet marble blocks and slabs; Denizli (Kaklık, Honaz, and Pamukkale basin) is the country's primary travertine hub; Burdur supplies high-volume cream beige marble; and onyx deposits are quarried across central and western Anatolian pockets including Afyonkarahisar, Denizli, and Bilecik.

Türkiye's natural stone export strength is tracked nationally by the [Istanbul Mineral Exporters' Association (İMİB)](https://imib.org.tr/en/corporate/about-us/), with monthly volume breakdowns published in the [İMİB Export Statistics Center](https://imib.org.tr/en/veri-merkezi/export-statistics/). Afyonkarahisar's role as a primary block market is also reflected in the annual [Afyonkarahisar International Block Marble Expo](https://www.afyonblokmermer.com/en), where international buyers pair exhibition meetings with direct quarry inspections in İscehisar.

body.text: How do you schedule 4–6 quarry and slab-yard inspections in 3 days?

You can inspect 4 to 6 quarries and processing yards in 3 days by running a one-way north-to-south corridor—starting in Afyonkarahisar on Day 1, driving 2.5 hours southwest to Denizli on Day 2, and finishing in Burdur on Day 3 before descending 1.5 to 2 hours to Antalya Airport (AYT). Limit each day to two substantive sites so you inspect slabs in natural daylight.

High-elevation quarries in Afyonkarahisar and Burdur often sit 30 to 45 minutes up unpaved haul roads from the main highway, and winter snow or heavy rain can pause bench extraction. Schedule quarry bench visits for late morning when overhead sunlight reveals true veining and hairline fissures, and save indoor gangsaw, resin-line, and polishing-floor walkthroughs for afternoon slots.
What container loading and slab-crating checks prevent breakage?

Preventing marble and travertine breakage in 20-foot heavy-duty containers comes down to verifying kiln-dried, ISPM 15 heat-treated wooden A-frame bundles, foam or nylon inter-slab spacers, steel strapping tension, balanced axle weight distribution under 27 metric tons, and rigid diagonal timber bracing against container corner posts.

International wood-packaging rules are governed by the [IPPC ISPM 15 Wood Packaging Standard](https://www.ippc.int/publications/regulation-wood-packaging-material-international-trade-0), and Türkiye's national compliance framework is documented in the [IPPC Türkiye ISPM 15 Implementation Notice](https://www.ippc.int/en/countries/republic-turkiye/implementationispm/2025/03/regulation-of-wood-packaging-material-in-international-trade-2/)—requiring solid wood crates and dunnage to be heat-treated to a core temperature of at least 56°C for 30 minutes and stamped legibly on opposite sides. Review this pre-shipment yard checklist during factory audits:

items: Bundle tagging: Photograph and physically sign or spray-mark selected block numbers and sequential slab bundles before resin-filling and polishing.
Resin and fiberglass mesh: Confirm back-netting quality on fragile travertine, violet marble, and onyx slabs to prevent transit cracking.
ISPM 15 stamp check: Inspect timber A-frames, crates, and bracing blocks for clear, legible heat-treatment marks required by destination customs.
Moisture and spacer sheets: Ensure protective plastic or foam sheets sit cleanly between polished faces to stop abrasion and iron staining.

Container weight and lashing: Verify gross cargo weight stays within your destination road-weight limit (often 21–24 tons for North America) and require step-by-step loading photos before container sealing.

body.text: Which airports (Kütahya Zafer, Denizli, Antalya) save drive time?

Flying into [Kütahya Zafer Airport (KZR)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zafer_Airport) puts you roughly 45 to 60 minutes from Afyonkarahisar's İscehisar marble yards, [DHMİ Denizli Çardak Airport (DNZ)](https://dhmi.gov.tr/sayfalar/havalimani/cardak/GenelBilgiler.aspx) sits 35 minutes from Kaklık's travertine factories, and Antalya Airport (AYT) is 1.5 to 2 hours south of Burdur's beige quarries—making an open-jaw flight (KZR or DNZ inbound, AYT outbound) the fastest routing.

Because Zafer Airport has limited daily domestic frequencies from Istanbul, many international buyers fly into Denizli (DNZ) for Afyon–Denizli–Burdur loops or fly directly into Antalya (AYT) from Europe or the Gulf and drive north to Burdur first. faq.q: When is the best time of year to visit marble quarries in Afyon, Denizli, and Burdur?
faq.a: April through November offers the most reliable road access and clear daylight for outdoor block and slab inspections. High-altitude quarries in Afyonkarahisar and Burdur can experience snow closures between December and March, though indoor slab factories remain open year-round.

faq.q: What is the minimum order quantity for Turkish marble or travertine slabs?
faq.a: Most direct stone factories set a minimum of one 20-foot container (roughly 380 to 450 square meters of 2 cm slabs, or 250 to 300 square meters of 3 cm slabs), often allowing buyers to mix 2 to 4 compatible stone selections in one container.

faq.q: Should buyers inspect rough blocks or finished slabs?
faq.a: Distributors with their own gangsaw plants buy rough blocks directly at the quarry bench, while architectural contractors and slab wholesalers typically inspect finished, resin-filled, and polished slab bundles at the processing factory.

faq.q: Why are 20-foot containers used instead of 40-foot containers for natural stone?
faq.a: Natural stone is extremely dense—roughly 2.6 to 2.7 tons per cubic meter—so a 20-foot container hits maximum legal payload weight long before filling the volume of a 40-foot container.

faq.q: How can I make sure the slabs shipped match the bundles I approved?
faq.a: Mark your initials and purchase-order reference directly on the edge of the approved bundles during your yard visit, record sequential slab photos, and require pre-loading and container-sealing photographs tied to those bundle numbers.
